scope: Static local exported-image filesystem/package/advisory review only. No exploit, database query, image binary or privileged tool was executed. This is a base-image comparison, not final Bessemer artifact qualification or vulnerability suppression.

bookworm_comparison.interpretation: Trixie has zero CRITICAL scanner findings and no longer reports SQLite CVE-2025-7458, CVE-2026-11822 or CVE-2026-11824. Nine unique HIGH findings remain, including three new util-linux advisory IDs. Changes in package versions/components and scanner mapping explain why raw HIGH rows increase from 36 to 45 despite fewer unique HIGH IDs. Not an image-clean result.

vulnerabilities.title: ncurses: ncurses: Buffer overflow vulnerability may lead to arbitrary code execution.
vulnerabilities.assessment: infocmp is installed. Bessemer HTTP core and examples do not invoke this terminal-analysis tool; no package fix is recorded. Arbitrary application subprocess usage is outside this review.

vulnerabilities.title: sqlite: sqlite: Denial of service via heap-based buffer overflow in FTS5
vulnerabilities.assessment: SQLite 3.46.1 and CPython _sqlite3 are present; actual libsqlite SHA 317d80bf5d592f98a71e14d2330591d6a339f631f37c5977835af748a1f26715 contains ENABLE_FTS5. The HIGH FTS5 heap-overflow/denial-of-service finding remains unresolved. Current Bessemer core/basic/production examples expose no SQLite endpoint; applications accepting databases or SQL need separate review/remediation.

vulnerabilities.title: systemd: systemd-homed: Local privilege escalation via missing home-record signature verification
vulnerabilities.assessment: No systemd-homed daemon path exists in the exported base filesystem. Scanner maps source-package advisories onto installed libsystemd/libudev; this is component-level applicability evidence, not package remediation.

vulnerabilities.title: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions
vulnerabilities.assessment: libacl remains installed and affected in the scanner result. Current HTTP core/examples do not expose privileged ACL path operations. UID 10001, cap-drop ALL and no-new-privileges reduce the described privilege-escalation context only when independently verified on the final image/deployment.

vulnerabilities.title: util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
vulnerabilities.assessment: mount is present with mode 4755. Failed-helper privileged X-mount post-hooks require a local privileged/authorized mounting context. Exported /etc/fstab contains only the unconfigured comment. Final nonroot, cap-drop ALL and no-new-privileges deployment must be qualified; this base image alone is not a hardened deployment.

vulnerabilities.title: util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
vulnerabilities.assessment: nsenter is present with mode 0755. This issue requires a privileged operator to use --join-cgroup on an attacker-controlled target and pass root-opened cgroup authority across exec/credential changes. Bessemer core/examples do not run nsenter. Privileged maintenance/container configurations need their own assessment.

vulnerabilities.title: util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
vulnerabilities.assessment: mount is present with mode 4755. Advisory requires Linux 6.15+ and a local fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry. Exported /etc/fstab contains only the unconfigured comment. Conditional mitigation depends on preserving the final nonroot/cap-drop/no-new-privileges deployment and fstab policy; package remains unfixed.

vulnerabilities.title: util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
vulnerabilities.assessment: mount is present with mode 4755. Restricted bind-mount X-mount owner/group/mode redirection requires authorized mounting context; exported /etc/fstab is unconfigured. Conditional mitigation depends on final nonroot/cap-drop/no-new-privileges deployment and unchanged fstab policy; package remains unfixed.

vulnerabilities.title: perl-Archive-Tar: perl-Archive-Tar: Denial of Service via crafted tar header with large entry size
vulnerabilities.assessment: No Archive/Tar.pm exists in the exported base filesystem. The perl-base package alone does not establish the affected Archive::Tar module is installed.
